summary: A small game on the iDrive 6 screen, steered with the pedal and the wheel
author: inotbarnacle (packaged by NBTApps)
description:
A small game under My Vehicle: a jet over a scrolling five-lane road, moved by the car's own controls.

What it does
- The accelerator pedal sets how far up the screen the jet flies, and the road scrolls faster with it
- The steering wheel moves the jet between lanes
- Traffic cones and police cars pass by
- It reads the pedal and the steering angle only while its page is open, and changes nothing in the car

What you need
- An NBT Evo head unit with iDrive 6 (ID6), on a software version the app was built for (see Good to know)
- NBTApps agent 1.6.0 or later
- The car's diagnostic gateway at 169.254.21.3, which is where the app looks for it

After installing
The iDrive screen restarts. Open My Vehicle and choose Road Jet.

Good to know
- It is not something to play while driving
- The page is laid out for a 1280×480 screen only. On another screen it does not fit
- Without the diagnostic gateway it falls back to the car's MOST bus, where it has the pedal only and the jet stays in the middle
- The pedal and steering readings are set up for the author's car. Another engine or steering system may need its own
- This package does not check the head unit's software version. The author's own installer accepts only these NBTevo versions: L17252I, M17365I, N18032I, N18092I, P18362I, Q18491I, R19144I, S19322I, T18501I, U19384I, V20153I, X20511I, Y21432J, Y22292I, Y23236I and Y24073J. On another version the menu may not load
- If the app was put on this car before, with the author's desktop installer or by hand, uninstall it the same way first. NBTApps refuses to install over it
- A car whose diagnostic gateway has another address needs a gateway-ip.txt file in the app's folder on the head unit. This package does not write one
- This is a pre-release: the package has not yet been installed on a car through NBTApps

Road Jet is by inotbarnacle, free of charge under the MIT License. NBTApps packages the author's own builds, unchanged, with the author's agreement. It comes as it is: you install it at your own risk.
